claim: Shared pessimistic Bellman targets across ensemble members can make a nominally pessimistic LCB (mean minus standard deviation) estimator produce effectively optimistic value estimates.
scope_conditions: offline RL, ensemble-based Q-function pessimism, D4RL/RL Unplugged benchmarks
quoted_support: shared pessimistic targets can paradoxically lead to value estimates that are effectively optimistic.

claim: The mechanism behind nominal-vs-effective pessimism mismatch in this paper is target independence versus sharing within one Q-ensemble, not sigma-scale differences across surrogate model classes.
scope_conditions: offline RL Q-ensembles, no surrogate-class comparison performed
quoted_support: the equations for the pessimistic LCB value estimate for Independent Targets... [versus] Shared Targets (Method 2) does the reverse... become positive, i.e. a negative penalty, yielding an effectively optimistic LCB estimate.

claim: This paper never compares a Q-ensemble against a competing surrogate class (e.g., Gaussian process); the term Gaussian process and surrogate do not appear.
quoted_support: gaussian process: 0 hits; surrogate: 0 hits; Bayesian optimization: 0 hits

claim: Ensemble-size sensitivity in this paper is contingent on the pessimism-construction method (shared vs independent targets), not on ensemble size alone.
scope_conditions: D4RL Gym and antmaze domains, N in {1,4,16,64}
quoted_support: In the Gym domains, Figure 5 demonstrates that increasing the number of ensembles from 4 to 64 does not result in a noticeable change in performance.

claim: With ensemble size increased from 4 to 64, the Shared-Min baseline's performance degrades on 7 of 12 D4RL Gym settings while MSG (independent targets) remains stable.
stance_target: pessimism-construction method interacts with ensemble size
quoted_support: we observe the performance of Shared-Min drops significantly on 7/12 D4RL Gym settings. In constrast, the performance of MSG is stable and does not change.
